### **Organization Overview:**


**Inspire Together** is a nonprofit organization committed to empowering underserved youth, individuals, and families by providing access to supportive services, resources, and opportunities that foster long\-term stability and success. We believe in creating pathways toward independence through housing, employment, and personal development programs that inspire growth and transformation.


### **Position Overview:**


Under the supervision of the **Program Supervisor**, the **Housing Navigator** plays a key role in connecting individuals and families to stable, affordable housing. This position is responsible for locating permanent housing options, developing strong relationships with landlords and property management companies, and supporting clients through the entire housing process — from application to move\-in.


The Housing Navigator collaborates closely with Case Managers and other service providers to ensure that clients are prepared for and able to maintain long\-term housing stability.


### **Key Responsibilities:**

* Identify and secure permanent housing opportunities for participants referred by Case Managers.
* Build and maintain partnerships with landlords, property owners, and housing agencies to expand available housing resources.
* Assist clients with housing applications, lease agreements, and move\-in coordination.
* Support participants with budgeting, financial planning, and understanding tenant responsibilities.
* Maintain an updated list of available affordable and supportive housing options.
* Coordinate with Case Managers, employment specialists, and community partners to ensure a holistic support plan.
* Advocate for clients experiencing barriers to housing, such as credit issues, low income, or past evictions.
* Conduct housing inspections and follow up to ensure clients are maintaining stable housing.
* Keep accurate documentation of housing activities and client progress in compliance with program standards.
* Attend staff meetings, trainings, and outreach events as required.

### **Qualifications \& Requirements:**

* **Education:** Bachelor’s degree in Social Work, Human Services, or a related field — or at least two (2\) years of equivalent social service experience.
* **Experience:** Prior experience working with homeless or low\-income individuals, youth, or families preferred.
* Strong knowledge of affordable housing programs, local housing resources, and community services.
* Ability to advocate effectively on behalf of clients and build positive relationships with landlords.
* Excellent communication, organizational, and time management skills.
* Valid **California Driver’s License** and proof of automobile insurance required.
* Must pass a **background check** and **fingerprint clearance**.
* CPR/First Aid certification (or willingness to obtain within 30 days of employment).

### **Work Environment:**


This position is **in\-person** at our San Bernardino office. Occasional travel within the community may be required for outreach, housing visits, or meetings with landlords and partners.

jobs.description:
**OUR EXCITING OPPORTUNITY**




*Community Action Partnership* has an exciting opportunity for




***Community Health Worker***




In this role, the Community Health Worker (CHW) will assist the CalAIM Housing Navigation and/or the Enhanced Care Management programs and Family Resource Centers by providing support to participants. The CHW will act as an intermediary between their participants and healthcare and/or social services providers, playing a critical part in the work and dedication of Community Action Partnership of Orange County’s initiatives. It’s leadership with a cause and the rewards are immeasurable!




**WHO WE ARE**


Born out of the War on Poverty more than 50 years ago, Community Action Partnership Orange County (CAP OC) is a trusted resource for Orange County community members who face obstacles such as food insecurity, unemployment, economic turmoil and more. We walk alongside the people we serve, and we act to meet immediate needs without delay. Our programs help empower people to improve their lives and their communities. We see poverty as an unacceptable reality for our neighbors and rally with key partners to help facilitate change.


CAP OC hires professionals who support and embody the following **EPIC** values:




Going above and beyond in every interaction and activity we undertake. We strive for **EXCELLENCE** in service, keeping a pulse on the most up to date innovations within our industry. Together we continually assess and improve the way to work and enhance the strategies we utilize to meet the needs of our community.


Reaching our goals by working collaboratively with each other and our community. We are working to do the things that have not been done: empowering families and individuals to financial independence, breaking the cycle of poverty, creating financial equity, combating food insecurity, and establishing healthy and energy\-efficient living conditions for all through social innovation. All of this takes **PROACTIVENESS**, and an intrinsic motivation that drives us to go above and beyond to create cutting\-edge trends and program designs. We have the will and the energy and won't stop until the needs of our underserved community no longer exist.




We are a team of high **INNOVATION**. We value the work we do; the people we serve; and treat each other with respect and kindness. We also have an environment of engaging in social economic justice by sharing of ideas and not afraid to try new things that increases our educational capacity. We think outside of the box, and challenge prevailing assumptions about issues of poverty.




Reaching our goals by working in partnership with each other and our community. The work we do is deeply rooted in the **COLLABORATION** we have with our community and its citizens. We care about the legacy of community action partnership and go above and beyond to ensure we support each other in bringing forth the services and resources that will positively change generations forever.




We have remained true to our mission “*We seek to end poverty by stabilizing, sustaining and empowering people with the resources they need when they need them. By forging strategic partnerships, we form a powerful force to improve our community.**”*

**VALUES**


In addition to our EPIC values our external values are as follows:

**Leadership**

We are guiding critical shifts in how people think and act to address the root causes of poverty

**Collaboration**

We bring together all capable partners to achieve transformative results


**Trust**

For over 50 years, the community has counted on us to empower those in need


**Compassion**

We treat each person we serve respectfully and with great care


**Justice**


We are passionate about advocating for those living in poverty and creating equity throughout the region




**WHAT YOU WILL ACCOMPLISH IN THIS ROLE**


The Community Health Worker will function as an integrated team member by providing support for the Housing Navigation, Enhanced Care Management programs, and Family Resource Centers. The Community Health Worker will provide support to the most vulnerable population, including but not limited to individuals experiencing homelessness, high utilizers, and/or youth involved in child welfare by helping them navigate their health and social needs.


*The salary for this position is $23\.00 \- $24\.00 per hour.*

*Required: Bilingual in English/Spanish, both written and oral forms.*

*The work schedule for the Community Health Worker does not allow for a remote or hybrid work schedule. Occasional evening and weekend hours may be required.*

* Collaborate with partners providing programs and services for participants of the FRCs and CAP OC.
* Assist with FRC programs and services including but not limited to front desk and in office coverage, food and diaper distributions, seasonal activities, senior programs, workshops, health education, etc.
* Play an active role within the Housing Navigation and ECM program by assisting members in completing forms, applications, and or intakes required to receive needed services or community resources. * Assist participants through BenefitsCal.com application process for Medi\-Cal and CalFresh

**Cat Program Director Job Summary**

This is a unique opportunity to contribute to a dynamic nonprofit cat rescue organization based in San Jose, CA. You will work closely with a committed Board of Directors, a passionate team of volunteers, and a small but dedicated staff to continue our lifesaving work.

The Cat Program Director oversees all aspects of The Dancing Cat’s cat and kitten programs, from intake through adoption and even beyond. This role coordinates foster placements, oversees medical care for the cats, advises on behavioral issues, contributes to adoption conversations, and supports our team of foster caregivers. The ideal candidate combines outstanding organizational and people\-management skills, and a very strong attention to detail, with hands\-on experience in cat welfare.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Intake**

Manage requests for intake from shelters, rescue partners, and the community; respond with advice, connect with rescue partners as relevant, prioritize those requests, and facilitate cats and kittens coming into The Dancing Cat based on ever\-changing capacity.

**Foster Family and Volunteer Support**

Plan, organize, manage, and lead the Cat foster care team. Support the Kitten foster team and act as a bridge between the two teams. Manage volunteer Foster Coordinators to ensure that all responsibilities are consistently carried out; provide leadership, accountability and performance feedback. Coordinate supply pickups from our adoption lounge 2\-3 days per week as scheduled.

**Adoption Coordination**

Support Lead Adoption Counselor with general advice and feedback when requested. Act as backup to the adoption team as needed.

**Medical Coordination**

Act as a backup to The Dancing Cat’s Vet Services Coordinator. Administer vaccines, dewormers, and other preventative treatments. Approve estimates for veterinary services up to the amount authorized by the Board of Directors.

**Administrative duties / Data \& Reporting**

Track program data and key metrics (intake numbers, live release rate, average length of stay, foster capacity) Maintain accurate, up\-to\-date records in The Dancing Cat's tracking systems. Provide periodic reports to the Board, funders and other ad hoc requests. Manage personnel issues as needed. Meet with staff and operational volunteers weekly or as needed.

**Program Development**

Identify gaps in foster capacity, medical resources, or process efficiency. Review and improve Standard Operating Procedures for intake, fostering, and adoption workflows. Support special initiatives (e.g., Trap Neuter Return coordination, shelter and rescue partnerships).

Professionally represent The Dancing Cat at all times.

**Requirements**

Successful candidates must have extensive cat knowledge and experience in a professional environment.

* Live in or relocate to the San Jose, CA area.
* Education: Bachelor’s degree.
* Experience: Minimum of three years of experience in a leadership position with strong and transferable skills.
* Technology: must be comfortable with a variety of software tools and be able to use them effectively.
* Ability to work with and around cats: Allergic conditions which would be aggravated when handling or working near/with cats may be a disqualification.
* Valid driver’s license for California is a requirement for continued employment and will be verified. Maintaining a satisfactory driving record is an ongoing condition of employment.

**Nature of Employment**

The Cat Program Director reports to the President of the Board of Directors. It is an exempt position, which requires a minimum of 40 hours per week and may include weekend, night, and holiday work. There is no minimum period of employment guaranteed or implied by acceptance of an employment offer. It is the policy of The Dancing Cat that employment for this position is at will, which means that employment is for no specified term and the employee or The Dancing Cat may terminate that employment at any time without cause.

Closing date: Applications will be reviewed as they are received. Applications received after September 15, 2026 may not be considered.

The Dancing Cat is a non\-profit organization founded in 2015\. We have rescued and found homes for over 2100 homeless cats. Our goal is to provide a lifeline to cats in need in the San Jose/South Bay area. The Dancing Cat has a cat adoption lounge located in downtown San Jose and has over 80 foster homes for cats and kittens in the South Bay.
